explanation: The theorem says that the antipodal map of S² acts as −1 on its second integral singular homology. I found nothing like it in Mathlib. Grepping Mathlib's AlgebraicTopology directory found no mention of antipodal maps. Mathlib/AlgebraicTopology/SingularHomology does not mention spheres. `integralSingularChainMap` does not occur anywhere in Mathlib, so it is defined in this library or another Formal Frontier library. Mathlib has no computation of the singular homology of spheres or of the degree of the antipodal map. The proof applies the library's own Mayer–Vietoris lemma (`integralSingularHomologyMap_eq_neg_id_of_twoOpen_swap`), not a Mathlib result.
